report.verdict: Diversification carried the top line, mix ate the margin: Q3-26 net revenue +19% to €1,220m (~$1.34bn) but only +4% on a comparable basis, adj. EBITDA €396m (~$436m) +6% reported / +2% comparable, and margin -410bps to 32.5% as an 18%-margin PrizePicks, €9m of LottoItalia amortisation and a €12m jump in corporate costs diluted a record-jackpot comp. The real news is in the guidance wording — the "~37%" FY adj. EBITDA margin target of Q1/Q2 has quietly become "within consensus" (€1,769–1,891m / ~$1.95–2.08bn, i.e. ~35.6% at the midpoint) — while Brazil's closure, a UK National Lottery still shrinking online and 3.5x leverage leave the shares at a 52-week low despite a reaffirmed €1.00/share (~$1.10) distribution floor.
summary: **Headline: revenue +19%, adj. EBITDA +6%, margin -410bps.** Q3-26 net revenue €1,220m (~$1.34bn) vs €1,023m, but only +4% on the company's comparable basis (PrizePicks in both periods, LottoItalia amortisation adjusted); adj. EBITDA €396m (~$436m) vs €374m, +2% comparable; margin 32.5% vs 36.6%. Investing.com cites revenue consensus of ~€1.23bn, so the top line was in line; management did not publish a quarterly EBITDA consensus, only a FY range.

**Operating EBITDA +13% to €341m (~$375m) as add-backs fall away.** EBITDA adjustments dropped to €55m (~$61m) from €73m (Q1-26 peak ~€107m): UK transition costs now nil, PrizePicks transaction/retention €9m, IWG acquisition accounting €3m — but the 'Allwyn brand initiative' is now €32m/quarter and the single largest add-back, which looks recurring in all but name.

**Guidance: revenue reaffirmed, margin target retired.** FY26 net revenue growth of 'mid-to-high 20%s' before c.€60m (~$66m) of Continental Europe one-offs is unchanged. However, the '~37% adj. EBITDA margin' language in the Q1 and Q2 releases has been replaced by 'within the range of consensus expectations' (company-compiled €1,769–1,891m / ~$1.95–2.08bn as of 13 Nov). At the midpoint (€1,830m) on €5.14bn revenue (+25%) that is ~35.6% — a ~140bps walk-down. Hitting 37% would need Q4 adj. EBITDA of ~€605m (+22% YoY), above the top of the consensus range.

**North America is the division that moved the margin.** PrizePicks net revenue +29% cFX (+24% reported) to €183m (~$201m), NA adj. EBITDA +26% pro forma to €43m (~$47m), but at a 17.8% margin; consolidating an 18%-margin DFS business against a 44%-margin European lottery base is mechanically dilutive. Add CE -270bps (LottoItalia) and corporate & eliminations at -€28m vs -€16m (+75%; corporate costs +€6m, rest eliminations) and the 410bps is fully explained.

**Comparable growth of 4% sits below the 'high single-digit' medium-term framing** that Barclays challenged on the call; the CFO declined to re-steer, citing record Q3-25 jackpots (Tzoker in Greece/Cyprus at an all-time high in Aug-25, EuroMillions in Austria/UK) and 'exceptionally customer-friendly' sports outcomes in August–September. Strong July margins (World Cup latter stages) were more than offset. Customer-friendly results continued into October and are 'factored in' to the outlook.

**Product mix: lottery down, iGaming and DFS up.** Lottery €513m (~$564m) -7%; sports betting €130m (~$143m) +1% (stakes up, win margin down); iGaming €151m (~$166m) +26%; DFS incl. prediction markets €183m (~$201m); VLTs & casinos €142m (~$156m) +2%; non-gaming €101m (~$111m) +20%. NGR €1,119m (~$1.23bn) +19%. Online NGR €530m (~$583m) +55%; online now 47% of NGR (37% LY, 45% comparable) and 54% of online-eligible NGR.

**Continental Europe (62% of net revenue): +3% against a +10% GGR comp.** Net revenue €754m (~$829m); Austria +10%, Czech Republic +4%, Greece & Cyprus broadly flat. Adj. EBITDA €328m (~$361m) -3%, flat excluding the €9m LottoItalia amortisation step-up; margin 43.5% (-270bps). Online NGR +8% to €226m (~$249m), 32% of segment NGR. Eurojackpot online (Greece, Aug) reached one-in-three online players in month one.

**United Kingdom: profit inflecting, demand still shrinking.** GGR €883m (~$971m) -11% cFX; online NGR -9% to €121m (~$133m); net revenue €237m (~$261m) -6% cFX. Adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m) via the licence cost-recovery mechanism (live since Q2), CAPEX down to €10m from €38m, transformation adjustments now nil. Powerball (July) has 1.3m+ players; new leadership team being installed. CFO: 'not going to say that we're happy with the performance'.

**Betano (36.75% equity-accounted): growth intact, Brazil shut.** Total revenue €795m (~$875m) +17% cFX / +21% reported; Allwyn's share of net income €35m (~$39m) +3% — profit growth lagged revenue on customer-friendly sports results. Brazil, Betano's largest market, closed on 25 Sep 2026 under a provisional measure; four new country launches planned for early 2027 (Spain confirmed; CEO of Allwyn Digital said five). Betano paid €150m (~$165m) post-quarter (Allwyn ~€55m / ~$61m), taking 2026 dividends to Allwyn to ~€258m (~$284m), +40% vs €184m; CFO expects 'material' dividends in 2027 'in any scenario'.

**Cash flow was the weak line.** Free cash flow €84m (~$92m) vs €215m: working-capital inflow €45m vs €152m, net finance costs paid €138m vs €70m (coupon timing, higher gross debt), tax paid €102m. Adj. EBITDA less CAPEX +14% to €345m (~$380m) as CAPEX fell 29% to €51m (4.2% of net revenue vs 7%). IFRS net cash from operations €88m vs €213m.

**Balance sheet: 3.5x and 'above target'.** Net debt incl. leases €6,641m (~$7.3bn) on pro forma LTM adj. EBITDA of €1,876m (~$2.06bn; look-through €1,793m plus €83m pre-acquisition PrizePicks); cash €1,941m (~$2.1bn) plus €215m of Austrian money-market assets; undrawn committed facilities €936m (~$1.0bn); nothing material matures before the USD 7.875% notes in 2029. TLB due 2032 repriced -50bps to E+250 in July (€24m modification gain). CFO: 'no scenario' of a covenant issue, covenants undisclosed.

**Capital returns: €1.19/share (~$1.31) in 2026.** €150m (~$165m) buyback completed 5 Oct (11.34m shares, ~1.4% of issued capital; treasury now 5.56%); €0.20 (~$0.22) interim paid 12 Nov, completing the €1.00/share (~$1.10) FY26 minimum. Scrip take-up only 15.4m shares (2% of shares, 10% of free float). The €1.00 floor was explicitly reaffirmed for 2027 even if Brazil stays closed and leverage drifts toward 4x — funded by Betano and LottoItalia (~€100m/yr net to Allwyn) dividends.

**Technology and content in-sourcing accelerates.** Post-quarter: perpetual global licence to Kambi's sportsbook source code for €50m (~$55m) over three years to 2029 (~half in 2027, capitalised) plus 'low tens of millions' of incremental annual opex from 2027; sportsbook is 13% of NGR and management flagged US sportsbook optionality. Remaining 30% of IWG acquired for USD 122m (€107m), payable Q1-27. Next Lotto (Germany) to 64.53% in October, consolidated from Q4. Australian casinos sold for €63m (~$69m), €3m gain. Brussels casino concession lost from July 2027 (<1% of CE adj. EBITDA).

**Below the line is noisy and flattered.** Adj. profit attributable €141m (~$155m) +5%; adj. EPS €0.18 (~$0.20) vs OPAP's historical €0.36 — not comparable (765.7m vs 358.6m weighted shares). Reported EPS €0.03 (~$0.03); IFRS profit €37m after €82m of PPA amortisation (D&A €158m reported vs €76m adjusted) — CFO says assume the Q3 run-rate until the PPA is finalised. Adj. tax rate 20% vs 35% on a deferred-tax benefit lifted adj. PAT +25%; NCI €45m vs €15m (PrizePicks minorities).

**Licence calendar is the next structural watch-point.** Austria's exclusive lottery licence extended from Sep-27 to end-2028; tender expected 2027, €40m (~$44m) fee on award for a 15-year term, bid coordinated with 30%+ partner ÖBAG. Greece legacy-games licence due 2030 ('110% attention'; Allwyn is Athens-listed).

**Governance and reporting.** Allwyn AG (Euronext Athens: ALWN) was formed on 24 Mar 2026 from the OPAP/Allwyn International combination; KKCG holds 79.28%, free float 20.72%. Petra Ehmann proposed as INED to lift board independence to 50%. All Q3 figures are preliminary, unaudited and on a 'look-through' non-IFRS basis; IFRS statements follow 26 Nov 2026.

**Share price: a relief bounce off the low.** ALWN +0.7% intraday to €9.63 (~$10.6) vs €9.56 prior close (range €9.52–9.71), one day after a 52-week low of €9.43; -50% from the €19.03 January high and -21.5% over the past month following the Brazil ban.

**Thesis read-through.** Diversification is delivering top-line resilience, but the earnings algorithm is migrating to a lower-margin, more acquisitive model (DFS, in-sourced tech, minority buy-ins) while the two cash engines that fund the €1/share floor — Betano and the UK — face regulatory and execution risk respectively. FY26 margin is heading to ~35.5%, leverage is stuck around 3.5x, and the equity is pricing the Brazil downside; the Q4 lottery seasonality and PrizePicks' NFL/NBA quarter are the near-term support.

segments.name: Continental Europe (Austria, Czech Republic, Greece & Cyprus, Italy, Germany, Slovakia)
segments.headline: +3% net revenue against a +10% GGR comp; EBITDA flat ex-LottoItalia; iGaming +26% and online +8% carry a -8% lottery line.
narrative: Continental Europe remains the earnings engine, at €754m (~$829m) of net revenue (62% of group) and €328m (~$361m) of adj. EBITDA (83% of group). Net revenue grew 3% year-on-year, both reported and in constant currency, on a comparative in which segment GGR had risen 10% and Tzoker in Greece/Cyprus hit a record jackpot in August 2025. Austria led with +10%, the Czech Republic added 4% and Greece & Cyprus were broadly stable. GGR was €1,161m (~$1.28bn), +1%, with gaming taxes and good-cause contributions of €462m (~$508m) absorbing 40% of GGR (+2%); non-gaming revenue jumped 38% to €55m (~$61m), so NGR itself was only +1% at €699m (~$769m). Sequentially net revenue was +3.1% versus Q2's €731m, which had carried the higher Austrian gaming-tax rate for a full quarter.

By product, iGaming was the engine at €151m (~$166m), +26% year-on-year and +2.7% quarter-on-quarter, while sports betting net revenue was €130m (~$143m), +1% year-on-year but -10% quarter-on-quarter: management said amounts staked were higher but win margins were materially lower, with strong July margins through the World Cup final stages more than offset by exceptionally customer-friendly outcomes in August and September; Q3-25 margins had also been weak, so the comp was not a high one. Lottery net revenue fell 8% to €276m (~$304m) on the Tzoker jackpot cycle, and VLTs & casinos were +2% at €142m (~$156m). The CFO's own benchmark on the call was telling: in the Czech Republic and Austria the group runs roughly €450m of iGaming against ~€30m of sports revenue, against a 'good proposition' norm of 50/50 — which is the real strategic rationale for the Kambi deal and implies sportsbook is a long way from scale in these markets.

Digital was again the structural driver: online NGR rose 8% to €226m (~$249m), 32% of segment NGR (30% last year) and 41% of online-eligible NGR. Eurojackpot online launched in Greece in August and reached one in three online players in its first month, following the Lotto revamp and Eurojackpot's retail introduction over the past three years; Greece's first Eurojackpot jackpot winner (€38m) was drawn this week, which should help Q4 awareness. Smaller innovations (Keno upgrade in the Czech Republic, a gold-prize scratchcard in Austria) continue, and in October the group moved Next Lotto (German online lottery reseller) to a 64.53% controlling stake for ~€10m (~$11m) after a €3m capital contribution lifted the interest to 46.29% at quarter-end; it consolidates from Q4.

Profitability held but did not grow. Adj. EBITDA fell 3% to €328m, a 43.5% margin versus 46.2% (-270bps year-on-year, though +340bps quarter-on-quarter on seasonality and the Q2 tax drag). The entire decline is the €11m fall in share of profit of equity-method investees (€8m vs €19m), of which €9m is the higher licence-fee amortisation at LottoItalia (32.5% owned) under the Lotto licence renewed 30 November 2025 — a structural ~€36m annual drag on reported EBITDA, though the CFO stressed LottoItalia will keep distributing ~100% of free cash flow, about €100m a year net to Allwyn. Ex-LottoItalia, aggregate EBITDA across Austria, Czech and Greece & Cyprus was flat. Cost lines were well controlled apart from marketing, which rose 21% to €80m (~$88m), 10.6% of net revenue versus 9.1%; agents' commissions and materials were +3% and personnel/other -2%. Management declined to break out country-level EBITDA, but pointed to Greece & Cyprus (the largest sports book) as the market most hit by margins and to jackpot exposure driving the lottery lines. CAPEX was €15m (~$17m), -17%, so adj. EBITDA less CAPEX was €313m (~$344m), -2%.

Portfolio tidy-ups and regulation: the non-core Australian casino operations (held within this segment) were sold in August for AUD 103m (€63m / ~$69m) with a €3m gain; the Brussels casino concession was awarded to another operator from July 2027 (less than 1% of segment EBITDA in 2025). Austria's exclusive lottery licence has been extended to end-2028 with a tender expected in 2027 and a ~€40m (~$44m) fee on award for a 15-year term, bid alongside 30%+ partner ÖBAG; Greece's legacy-games licence falls due in 2030. For FY26 the segment carries c.€60m (~$66m) of previously flagged one-off revenue impacts (c.-2%). Our read: the segment is a mid-single-digit NGR grower with the lottery line now cycling tough jackpot comps into a seasonally strong Q4, and margin ambition should be reset to the low-40s rather than the mid-40s given LottoItalia amortisation and rising marketing intensity.

segments.name: North America (PrizePicks, Allwyn LS Group/Illinois, IWG) — presented on 100% basis
segments.headline: PrizePicks re-accelerated to +29% cFX with EBITDA +26% at a 17.8% margin; Packs adds a non-sports vertical; Q3 is the seasonal trough ahead of the NFL/NBA quarter.
narrative: North America is where the Q3 narrative turned. On the company's '100% basis' (PrizePicks in both years), net revenue rose 21% in constant currency (20% reported) to €242m (~$266m), of which PrizePicks net revenue was €183m (~$201m), +29% cFX (+24% reported) — a sharp re-acceleration from the +3% cFX printed in Q2, when sports outcomes had depressed DFS revenue. Customer activity (DFS entry fees plus real cash deployed in prediction-market contracts, explicitly not notional volume) grew more than 30% year-on-year across both products, and management said there was no material sports-outcome effect in the quarter; a World Cup boost in July was offset by the later NFL start. Segment GGR was €190m (~$209m), +30% cFX, and non-gaming revenue (Illinois private-management fees, B2B tech/content) was €59m (~$65m), +7% — the Illinois management fee and operating allowance are cost pass-throughs that depress the margin ratio but not absolute EBITDA. Sequentially net revenue fell 18% from Q2's €294m, reflecting the DFS calendar (NBA playoffs/MLB in Q2 vs a part-NFL Q3).

Adj. EBITDA rose 26% to €43m (~$47m) from a pro forma €34m, a 17.8% margin (+100bps year-on-year, but -1,760bps versus Q2's €104m / 35.4%, again seasonality). The driver was operating leverage on marketing: marketing services rose 14% to €75m (~$83m), 31% of net revenue versus 33%, with management describing a 'differentiated customer acquisition and retention model'; materials/consumables were +12% to €74m and personnel/other -2% at €65m. Operating EBITDA was €30m versus €5m as EBITDA adjustments halved to €13m (PrizePicks transaction and short-term retention costs €9m, IWG put-option accounting €3m, litigation €1m) from €29m — the CFO conceded that a 'significant part' of the Q1–Q3 cost dynamics in the non-marketing lines were these acquisition-related one-offs rather than run-rate. CAPEX was €13m (~$14m), +44%, leaving adj. EBITDA less CAPEX at €30m (~$33m), +20%. On a nine-month consolidated basis the segment has contributed €775m (~$853m) of net revenue and €222m (~$244m) of adj. EBITDA, a 28.6% margin — a useful reminder that Q3 is structurally the DFS low season.

Product-wise, DFS remains 'by a large way' the biggest line, with prediction markets reported inside DFS and PrizePicks acting as a broker earning a commission with no sports-outcome margin volatility — the CFO likened it to fee income in financial services. Ahead of the NFL season PrizePicks launched fully blended line-ups combining player, team and culture picks, and in October it launched 'Packs', a collectible trading-card product with physically deliverable graded cards and 'grail' inventory valued at up to $8m (a ~$3m Dylan Harper rookie card was pulled from a $25 pack). Management's pitch is that Packs is year-round, independent of sports outcomes, and already shows a majority of loyal DFS customers participating, reactivation of dormant players and new-audience acquisition; the financial logic is better retention, lower marketing per active and recycling of winnings. None of this is in Q3 numbers — the first Packs contribution lands in Q4. Trading commentary was constructive: monthly actives grew sequentially from the August low, October saw record customer activity with NFL/NHL/NBA all live, and month-to-date November actives are up double digits year-on-year. The group does not disclose actives, ARPU, handle or promotional intensity for PrizePicks, which limits the ability to separate price from volume; the 'leading position in DFS' claim rests on 24-month app-download data.

The segment also absorbs the M&A and technology agenda. The remaining 30% of IWG (digital e-Instants) was bought in October for USD 122m (€107m / ~$118m), payable in Q1-27 after a put-option exercise; and the Kambi agreement — a perpetual global licence to Kambi's sportsbook source code for €50m (~$55m) over three years to 2029, with a team transferring to Allwyn after a transition period — was explicitly framed as giving optionality for a US sportsbook 'if we strategically decide', since Kambi's platform is US-approved and used across 100+ jurisdictions. PrizePicks' own consideration was reported by NEXT.io at $1.6bn with up to a further $1bn contingent on performance; the Q3 pro forma run-rate (EBITDA +26%) is the first clean read-through on that earn-out. Our judgement is that the quarter de-risks the 'PrizePicks stalled' worry from H1 and that the 18% Q3 margin is a trough rather than a ceiling, but the group's blended margin will continue to drift lower as North America grows faster than Europe, and the Q4 marketing step-up around the NFL/NBA calendar is the swing factor for the FY EBITDA range.

Kambi deal: perpetual global sportsbook source-code licence for €50m (~$55m) over three years to 2029, team transferring; gives optionality for a US sportsbook 'if we strategically decide'.
PrizePicks consideration reported by NEXT.io at $1.6bn plus up to $1bn contingent; Q3 pro forma EBITDA +26% is first clean read-through on the earn-out.
Group blended margin will continue to drift lower as North America grows faster than Europe.

segments.name: United Kingdom (Allwyn UK — The National Lottery)
segments.headline: Profit doubled to €18m on licence cost-recovery, but GGR -11% cFX and online -9% as players 'adjust' to the new platform; Powerball is the offset, recovery timing undefined.
narrative: The UK delivered the quarter's clearest split between financial and operational performance. Revenue from gaming activities (GGR, i.e. National Lottery sales) fell 11% in constant currency (9% reported) to €883m (~$971m), with gaming taxes and good-cause contributions of €646m (~$711m) taking 73% of GGR. Net revenue — Allwyn's retained economics under the 4th licence — fell 6% cFX (5% reported) to €237m (~$261m), flat sequentially against Q2's €236m. The gap between the GGR and net-revenue declines reflects the licence's incentive model, including the recovery, since Q2, of a portion of the ~£450m technology-transformation investment. Management attributed the sales decline to a strong comparative with favourable EuroMillions jackpot cycles and to 'players continuing to adjust' to the new website and app introduced in Q1 — the CFO was blunter to NEXT.io, citing 'perceived frictions' not appreciated by part of the online base. Online NGR fell 9% to €121m (~$133m), 51% of segment NGR versus 53%, so the digital channel, which is the whole point of the re-platforming, is still shrinking faster than retail.

Powerball, launched in July as the first deployment of the game outside the US, has attracted more than 1.3m players and is the main offset; the enhanced Lotto format launched in Q2, £10 instant-win games are live, a £10 scratchcard pilot started in September (doubling the previous top prize), and quick-commerce scratchcard distribution now covers 1,700+ third-party stores. A new leadership team is being installed (NEXT.io reports Phil Walker as interim CEO, with an online-gaming background) 'to deliver the next stage of the transformation, especially in digital'. The CFO declined to give sales targets for 2027 and said plainly 'there's more still to be done in the UK, and I'm not going to say that we're happy with the performance' — the most candid language in the release cycle, and consistent with a business that is still operationally behind plan two and a half years into the licence.

Financially the segment has turned. Adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m) from €9m, a 7.6% margin versus 3.6% (+400bps), driven by the cost-recovery mechanism rather than trading; agents' commissions, materials and services fell 21% to €119m, personnel/other fell 10% to €38m and marketing was flat at €62m (~$68m), now 26.2% of net revenue versus 24.8%. Operating EBITDA was €18m versus a €5m loss, because transformation-related EBITDA adjustments fell from €14m to nil. CAPEX collapsed to €10m (~$11m) from €38m (and -€3m quarter-on-quarter) with the transformation complete, so adj. EBITDA less CAPEX swung to +€8m (~$9m) from -€29m — the single largest contributor to the group's +14% adj. EBITDA-less-CAPEX growth. Sequentially adj. EBITDA fell from Q2's €23m (9.7% margin). Nine-month adj. EBITDA is €45m (~$50m) on €697m (~$767m) of net revenue, a 6.5% margin, against FY25 segment adj. EBITDA of €34m.

Our read is that the UK is now a cash-neutral-to-positive but low-margin annuity whose upside depends on reversing the online participation loss; the cost-recovery mechanism provides an earnings floor but not growth, and the licence's good-causes ambition (NEXT.io cites a £60m/week pledge by the end of the ten-year term) requires sales momentum that is not yet visible. Q4 is the seasonally strongest lottery quarter and the first full quarter of Powerball with Christmas scratchcard demand; a stabilisation of online GGR in Q4 would be the first evidence the platform frictions are behind them. GBP figures are not converted to USD in this note.

segments.name: Betano (Kaizen Gaming) — 36.75% equity-accounted investee, 100% basis unless stated
segments.headline: Revenue +17% cFX to €795m but Allwyn's share of profit only +3%; Brazil — the largest market — shut on 25 Sep; dividends (+40% YTD) are the group's key funding line for the €1/share floor.
narrative: Betano is not consolidated — only Allwyn's 36.75% share of net income (€35m / ~$39m, +3%) sits in adj. EBITDA — but its cash matters more than its P&L line. Total revenue grew 17% in constant currency (21% reported) to €795m (~$875m), down 18% sequentially from Q2's World-Cup-boosted €972m, with sports-betting margins described as 'broadly similar' and customer-friendly in both periods. The mismatch between +17% revenue and +3% share of profit — after Q2's -3% on below-EBITDA items — prompted JPMorgan to ask for EBITDA granularity, which the CFO declined to provide beyond 'slightly slower growth in the quarter weighed on profitability year-on-year'. Nine-month share of net income is €156m (~$172m).

The regulatory event dominates. A provisional measure in force from 25 September 2026 closed Brazil's regulated online sports-betting and iGaming market; Betano's Brazilian operations stopped shortly before quarter-end, so Q3 carries only a 'small' impact and Q4 the full effect. Brazil was Betano's largest market in Q3 but operations across the other 20+ countries contribute the majority of revenue, and management repeatedly stressed the diversification: pre-existing expansion plans target four new countries in early 2027 (the release) or five (Allwyn Digital's CEO on the call), with Spain the only one named, taking the footprint toward 24 markets. Betano is 'ready to recommence operations as soon as the market opens' and is building mitigation plans for scenarios in which some or all regulated operations do not resume; Chile, where regulatory initiatives are also under way, was flagged by Piraeus Securities and is being 'monitored', with no revenue split disclosed. Management's argument that prohibition pushes activity offshore and reduces tax receipts is the standard industry line and offers no visibility on timing.

The dividend stream is the reason the €1.00/share minimum distribution survived unchanged. Betano received no dividend in Q3 (vs €55m received in Q3-25) but paid €150m (~$165m) after quarter-end — after the Brazilian measure — of which Allwyn's share is ~€55m (~$61m); with €551m distributed in H1, Betano's 2026 payout is €701m (~$771m), +40% on €501m, and Allwyn's share ~€258m (~$284m) versus €184m. The CFO's assertion that Betano has 'a material cash position, no debt, and many levers to optimise cash flow' and will deliver 'material dividend flows in 2027 in any scenario' is the central support for the capital-return commitment, alongside LottoItalia's ~€100m a year. Our view is that the quantum of 2027 dividends is the single biggest swing factor for Allwyn's leverage path: at Q3's run-rate Betano contributes roughly 9% of group adj. EBITDA but a far higher share of discretionary cash; a prolonged Brazilian closure would likely cut Betano's distribution capacity meaningfully even with cost mitigation, and the market's -21% one-month reaction suggests investors are not giving management the benefit of the doubt.

Strategically, the Kambi decision also says something about the Betano relationship: Allwyn chose to licence Kambi rather than lean on Betano's proprietary stack, explaining that Betano is focused on its own markets and new entries and that the in-house platform is for majority-owned brands. Betano therefore remains a financial investment with a strong operating team rather than a technology source — and its carrying value sits within the group's €4.8bn of equity-method investees on the balance sheet.

highlights.text: PrizePicks re-accelerated: net revenue +29% cFX to €183m (~$201m) from +3% in Q2, customer activity +30%+, NA adj. EBITDA +26% pro forma with marketing only +14% (31% of revenue); October set a record for activity and November MAU is up double digits — the H1 'PrizePicks has stalled' worry is answered.

Operating EBITDA +13% to €341m (~$375m) as EBITDA add-backs halved from the Q1 peak to €55m, UK transition costs went to nil and CAPEX normalised to 4.2% of revenue; adj. EBITDA less CAPEX +14% to €345m (~$380m), +11% comparable.

Digital mix shift continues: online NGR +55% to €530m (~$583m), 47% of NGR (54% of online-eligible); CE online +8%; iGaming +26%; Eurojackpot online reached one-in-three Greek online players in month one.

Capital returns delivered and defended: €1.19/share (~$1.31) in 2026 (€1.00 distributions + €150m buyback), and the €1.00 minimum explicitly reaffirmed for 2027 even in a Brazil-shut scenario, backed by Betano dividends +40% to ~€258m (~$284m) and ~€100m/yr from LottoItalia.

UK economics inflected: adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m), adj. EBITDA less CAPEX +€37m YoY to +€8m as the ~£450m transformation ended and cost recovery kicked in; Powerball already has 1.3m+ players.

Kambi perpetual source-code licence for €50m (~$55m) is a cheap route to owning the sportsbook stack behind 13% of NGR, with cross-sell into a €450m Czech/Austrian iGaming base and a US sportsbook option; IWG 100% and Next Lotto control tidy the structure.
Liquidity is not the issue: €1.94bn (~$2.1bn) cash plus €215m Austrian money-market assets, €936m (~$1.0bn) undrawn, no material maturity before 2029, and the 2032 TLB repriced 50bps tighter in July.

lowlights.text: The '~37% adj. EBITDA margin' FY26 target in the Q1 and Q2 releases has been replaced by 'within consensus' (€1,769–1,891m); the midpoint implies ~35.6% on mid-20s revenue growth, and 9M margin is 35.3%. This is a guidance cut in all but name and was not called out as such.

Comparable net revenue growth of 4% and comparable adj. EBITDA of +2% are below the high-single-digit medium-term framing; lottery -7%, sports betting +1% on weak win margins that persisted into October, and management would not re-steer 2027.

UK demand is still deteriorating: GGR -11% cFX, online NGR -9%, 'players continuing to adjust' to the new platform nine months after launch; the CFO is 'not happy' and gave no recovery timeline — the EBITDA doubling is a cost-recovery mechanic, not trading.

Brazil: Betano's largest market closed from 25 Sep with no visibility on reopening; Betano's share of profit (+3%) already lags revenue (+17%), Chile is a further regulatory risk, and 2027 Betano dividends are the swing factor for leverage and the €1/share floor.

Free cash flow -61% to €84m (~$92m) on a smaller working-capital inflow and €138m of net finance costs paid; net debt €6.64bn (~$7.3bn), 3.5x and 'above target', with €107m IWG, ~€25m Kambi and €40m Austria outflows still to come and ~€36m/yr of LottoItalia amortisation now structural.

Corporate & eliminations swelled 75% to -€28m and the 'Allwyn brand initiative' add-back is running at €32m a quarter (€130m annualised) — a recurring consumer-brand investment being excluded from adjusted EBITDA.

Earnings quality: adj. EPS €0.18 (~$0.20) is shown against OPAP's €0.36 on a share count that more than doubled; a deferred-tax benefit cut the adjusted tax rate to 20% from 35% and flattered adj. PAT (+25%); reported EPS is €0.03 after €82m of PPA amortisation on a still-unfinished purchase-price allocation.

forecast.intro: Revenue guidance is unchanged — FY26 consolidated net revenue growth of 'mid-to-high 20%s' on the FY25 look-through base of €4,112m (~$4.5bn), before c.€60m (~$66m) of one-off impacts in Continental Europe — which implies €5.14–5.30bn and a Q4 of €1.47–1.63bn, i.e. +31–46% on Q4-25's €1,119m with PrizePicks' strongest quarter (NFL/NBA plus the first Packs contribution) and Next Lotto consolidation doing the heavy lifting. The EBITDA framing has changed: Q1 and Q2 said 'adj. EBITDA margin of ~37%'; Q3 says 'within the range of consensus expectations' of €1,769–1,891m (~$1.95–2.08bn, company-compiled 13 Nov). With 9M adj. EBITDA at €1,297m (~$1.43bn), that range implies Q4 of €472–594m against €497m last year, and a FY margin of 34.4–36.8% — the midpoint (€1,830m, ~35.6%) is ~140bps below the old target. The division that moved it is North America (PrizePicks consolidated at an 18–35% seasonal margin against a 44% CE base), compounded by LottoItalia amortisation (€9m/quarter in CE), corporate costs/eliminations (+€12m YoY) and October's customer-friendly sports results, with Betano's Brazil closure feeding the share-of-profit line from Q4.

forecast.view: Our FY26 estimate is net revenue of ~€5.15bn (~$5.7bn), +25%, i.e. the lower half of guidance, built on Q4 of ~€1.48bn: CE +2–3% with Q4 lottery seasonality but a still-tough Tzoker/EuroMillions comp, UK -4–5% as online stabilises on Powerball and Christmas scratchcards, and a PrizePicks quarter in the €330–380m range with Packs incremental. We model FY26 adj. EBITDA of ~€1.83bn (~$2.0bn), a **~35.5% margin, roughly the consensus midpoint and 150bps below the retired 37% target**, which requires Q4 adj. EBITDA of ~€530m (+7% YoY) — PrizePicks' seasonal margin recovery and ~€20m of UK improvement against ~€9m of LottoItalia amortisation, a ~€10m higher corporate run-rate, weaker October sports margins and a Betano share-of-profit line likely down year-on-year with Brazil dark. Q4 is also the first quarter with Next Lotto consolidated (small). Cash: Q4 should be the strongest working-capital quarter and includes ~€55m from Betano, against €35m of residual buyback (October) and €149m of interim distribution cash (November); we expect **year-end net debt/EBITDA of ~3.4–3.5x**, with 2027 deleveraging dependent on Betano's payout — in a Brazil-stays-shut case we would not assume leverage falls below ~3.2x by end-2027 after the €1.00/share (~€760m) floor, IWG, Kambi and Austria. For 2027, the arithmetic that matters is PrizePicks' growth (and the earn-out), the UK's online recovery, and whether 'material' Betano dividends mean €150m or €250m to Allwyn; medium-term comparable growth of 4% needs to re-accelerate to the high single digits for the margin debate to become secondary. All figures above are our estimates.
watch: Brazil: whether the 25 Sep provisional measure lapses, is converted to law or amended; Betano's Q4 revenue run-rate ex-Brazil and the size/timing of its first 2027 dividend (Allwyn guided 'material in any scenario').

Q4 PrizePicks: first Packs revenue contribution, marketing spend around NFL/NBA (Q3 was 31% of revenue), MAU/activity growth and any state-level DFS/prediction-market enforcement; the implied earn-out trajectory on the reported $1.6bn + up to $1bn consideration.

UK: Q4 National Lottery GGR and online NGR trend (Q3: -11% cFX / -9%) with a full Powerball quarter and £10 scratchcard pilot; confirmation of the permanent UK CEO and any revised sales/good-causes plan.

FY26 landing versus the €1,769–1,891m consensus range and the FY27 margin framework — will management reinstate a margin target, and what is the run-rate of the €32m/quarter brand add-back and corporate costs?
Capital allocation sequencing: €1.00/share 2027 distribution timetable, any further buyback, IWG $122m (Q1-27), Kambi ~€25m (2027) and the Austrian licence tender (€40m fee on award; 15-year term).
26 Nov IFRS statements: finalised purchase-price allocation and PPA amortisation run-rate (€82m in Q3), NCI line, and reported leverage/covenant headroom disclosure.
Continental Europe sports margins in Q4 (October already customer-friendly), Tzoker jackpot cycle into year-end, and Eurojackpot online traction in Greece after the first €38m winner.
